require "minitest/autorun"

def slugify(title)
  title
    .unicode_normalize(:nfkd)
    .gsub(/\p{Mn}/, "")
    .downcase
    .gsub(/['’]/, "")
    .gsub(/[^a-z0-9]+/, "-")
    .gsub(/\A-+|-+\z/, "")
end

class SlugifyTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_basic_title
    assert_equal "hello-world", slugify("Hello, World!")
  end

  def test_collapses_runs_of_separators
    assert_equal "a-b-c", slugify("a  --  b___c")
  end

  def test_strips_leading_and_trailing_separators
    assert_equal "hello", slugify("  ...Hello...  ")
  end

  def test_transliterates_accents
    assert_equal "creme-brulee", slugify("Crème Brûlée")
  end

  def test_drops_apostrophes
    assert_equal "dont-stop", slugify("Don't Stop")
  end

  def test_keeps_digits
    assert_equal "top-10-tips", slugify("Top 10 Tips")
  end

  def test_empty_and_symbol_only
    assert_equal "", slugify("")
    assert_equal "", slugify("!!!")
  end
end

`slugify.rb` is written, with the method and Minitest tests in the same file; `ruby slugify.rb` runs them and all 7 pass.

Beyond the basic `"Hello, World!"` → `"hello-world"` case, it makes a few choices you didn't specify:

- **Accents:** accented letters are transliterated, so `"Crème Brûlée"` becomes `"creme-brulee"`.
- **Apostrophes:** they are dropped rather than turned into hyphens, so `"Don't Stop"` becomes `"dont-stop"`.
- **Non-Latin text:** characters with no ASCII equivalent (e.g. Chinese or Cyrillic) are removed, so a title made only of those gives an empty string.
